item.title: How Americans deceive ourselves about slavery
item.description: Clint Smith's How the Word Is Passed explores how slavery is — and isn't — taught. And Above Ground includes poems to his children about what their ancestors endured and escaped. He spoke with Fresh Air in 2021 and 2023.
item.content:encoded: Clint Smith's How the Word Is Passed explores how slavery is — and isn't — taught. And Above Ground includes poems to his children about what their ancestors endured and escaped. He spoke with Fresh Air in 2021 and 2023.
item.dc:creator: Terry Gross

item.title: As speed cameras spread to more states, so does the backlash from drivers
item.description: Millions of drivers across the country are encountering speed cameras for the first time, or will soon. Some don't like it, but advocates say there's clear evidence that cameras make roads safer.
item.content:encoded:

item.description: Just like all previous summers since the pandemic began, COVID-19 cases are ticking up again, even while other health threats make more headlines.

item.title: Mangione pleads guilty in federal court, leaving fate of state trial uncertain
item.description: Mangione has pleaded guilty to stalking charges in connection with the death of Brian Thompson, a health care executive. A separate judge will decide the future of Mangione's state trial.

item.title: The Taliban has taken a terrible toll on the education of girls -- and boys as well
item.description: Saturday marks the 5th anniversary of the current Taliban rule in Aghanistan. They've had a devastating impact on girls' education. A lesser told story is their impact on the education of boys.

item.title: From Europe to Asia, floods to heatwaves, world experiences weather shocks
item.description: At least eight people died in Japan as heavy rains flooded roads and disrupted traffic while firefighters from Britain to France and Croatia struggled to contain blazes in Europe's fifth heatwave this summer
